meaning: while; on the way; taking the opportunity of
structure: Verb-stem / Noun + がてら
usage: One outing serves two purposes; the main clause is usually a movement (行く, 寄る, 歩く). Compare 〜かたがた (formal, greetings and visits) and 〜かたわら (two long-term activities).

examples.japanese: 散歩がてら、駅前の本屋に寄って新刊をのぞいてきた。
examples.english: While out for a walk, I stopped by the bookstore in front of the station to look at the new releases.

examples.japanese: お客さんを駅まで送りがてら、郵便局で小包を出してきた。
examples.english: While seeing our guest off to the station, I also sent a parcel at the post office.

meaning: while also; alongside (one's main occupation)
structure: Verb-dict / Noun + の + かたわら
usage: Two activities pursued in parallel over a long period (a job and a side pursuit), not a one-off action. As a plain noun, かたわら also means 'beside'.

examples.japanese: 彼女は会社勤めのかたわら、週末は日本語教室でボランティアをしている。
examples.english: Alongside her office job, she volunteers at a Japanese class on weekends.

examples.japanese: 祖父は農業を営むかたわら、地元の歴史を研究して三冊の本にまとめた。
examples.english: While running a farm, my grandfather researched local history and compiled it into three books.

meaning: the moment; no sooner ... than
structure: Verb-dict + が早いか
usage: The second action follows almost instantly; it states a past fact, never a request or intention. Near-synonyms: 〜や否や (most formal), 〜なり (same subject, often surprising), 〜そばから (repeated).

examples.japanese: 子どもたちは玄関を開けるが早いか、ランドセルを放り出して遊びに行ってしまった。
examples.english: No sooner had the children opened the front door than they tossed their school bags aside and ran off to play.

examples.japanese: 開店のベルが鳴るが早いか、客たちは目当ての売り場へ駆け出した。
examples.english: The moment the opening bell rang, the customers dashed toward the counters they were after.

examples.japanese: 彼は給料をもらうが早いか、全部競馬につぎ込んでしまった。
examples.english: The minute he got his pay, he blew all of it on horse racing.

meaning: even; not even (an extreme example)
structure: Noun (+ particle) + すら
usage: A more literary 〜さえ. Unlike さえ, it is not used in the 〜さえ〜ば ('if only') construction.

examples.japanese: 高熱が三日も続き、水を飲むことすらつらかった。
examples.english: The high fever lasted three days, and even drinking water was hard.

examples.japanese: この漢字は、専門家ですら読み間違えることがある。
examples.english: Even specialists sometimes misread this kanji.

examples.japanese: 彼は長年連れ添った妻にすら、病気のことを打ち明けなかった。
examples.english: He didn't reveal his illness even to the wife he had been with for so many years.

meaning: nothing but; entirely; one ... after another
structure: Noun + ずくめ
usage: Works with a limited set of nouns (黒, いいこと, 規則, ごちそう, 結構). Unlike だらけ or まみれ it can be positive and does not mean physically covered.

examples.japanese: 昇進に結婚、新居の購入と、今年はいいことずくめの一年だった。
examples.english: A promotion, a wedding and a new home — this year brought nothing but good things.

examples.japanese: 黒ずくめの服を着た男が、店の前をうろうろしている。
examples.english: A man dressed all in black is loitering in front of the shop.

examples.japanese: 規則ずくめの寮生活に、入学早々うんざりしてしまった。
examples.english: Right after enrolling, I was already fed up with dorm life and its endless rules.

meaning: once ... (there's no going back); if ever ..., that's the end
structure: Verb-ta + ら最後 / Verb-ta + が最後
usage: The result is bad or irreversible and stated with certainty. 〜が最後 is slightly more literary.

examples.japanese: この子は一度泣き出したら最後、何をしても一時間は泣きやまない。
examples.english: Once this child starts crying, nothing will stop her for an hour.

examples.japanese: あの人に秘密を話したが最後、翌日には社内中に知れ渡っているだろう。
examples.english: If you ever tell him a secret, the whole company will know by the next day.

examples.japanese: この契約書に一度判を押したら最後、後から取り消すことはできない。
examples.english: Once you stamp your seal on this contract, you cannot cancel it later.

meaning: ever since
structure: Verb-te + からというもの
usage: Stresses a marked, lasting change that began with the event; more emotional than the neutral 〜て以来.

examples.japanese: 犬を飼い始めてからというもの、父は毎朝六時に起きるようになった。
examples.english: Ever since we got a dog, my father has been getting up at six every morning.

examples.japanese: 彼女は留学から戻ってからというもの、見違えるほど積極的になった。
examples.english: Ever since she came back from studying abroad, she has become remarkably outgoing.

examples.japanese: スマートフォンを手にしてからというもの、紙の本をほとんど読まなくなった。
examples.english: Ever since I got a smartphone, I've hardly read any paper books.

meaning: never cease to; sincerely; deeply (hope, respect, love)
structure: Verb-te + やまない
usage: Used with verbs of feeling such as 願う, 祈る, 愛する, 尊敬する, 期待する. Typical of speeches, letters and formal writing.

examples.japanese: 皆様のご健康とご多幸を心より願ってやみません。
examples.english: I sincerely wish you all good health and happiness.

examples.japanese: 恩師は、私が今も尊敬してやまない人物だ。
examples.english: My former teacher is someone I still deeply respect.

examples.japanese: この作家は、生涯故郷の海を愛してやまなかったという。
examples.english: This writer is said to have loved the sea of his hometown all his life.

meaning: combined with; coupled with
structure: Noun + と相まって / Noun + も相まって
usage: Two factors reinforce each other to produce a stronger effect. Also AとBが相まって and 〜も相まって.

examples.japanese: 色づいた紅葉が澄んだ秋空と相まって、息をのむような景色をつくり出していた。
examples.english: The red autumn leaves, together with the clear autumn sky, created a breathtaking view.

examples.japanese: 円安に規制緩和も相まって、訪日客の数は過去最高を記録した。
examples.english: The weak yen, coupled with deregulation, pushed the number of visitors to Japan to a record high.

examples.japanese: 誠実な人柄と確かな技術が相まって、彼の店は地元で厚い信頼を得ている。
examples.english: His sincere character combined with solid skills has earned his shop deep trust locally.

meaning: when it comes to; once (a certain level or stage) is reached
structure: Noun / Verb-dict + ともなると / Noun / Verb-dict + ともなれば
usage: The noun marks a notably high status, time or amount; the rest states what naturally comes with it.

examples.japanese: 大企業の社長ともなると、分刻みのスケジュールで動かなければならない。
examples.english: When you're the president of a big company, you have to work to a minute-by-minute schedule.

examples.japanese: 十二月ともなれば、この辺りの山はすっかり雪に覆われる。
examples.english: Come December, the mountains around here are completely covered in snow.

examples.japanese: 子どもが三人ともなると、毎月の食費だけでも相当な額になる。
examples.english: Once you have three children, the monthly food bill alone is considerable.

meaning: unique to; that only ... could offer
structure: Noun + ならではの + Noun / Noun + ならではだ
usage: Almost always praise. The literary AならではBない means 'only A can B'.

examples.japanese: 港町ならではの新鮮な魚介料理を、心ゆくまで味わった。
examples.english: We savored to our hearts' content the fresh seafood you can only get in a port town.

examples.japanese: 細部まで行き届いたこの仕上がりは、熟練の職人ならではだ。
examples.english: This finish, perfect down to the smallest detail, is something only a seasoned craftsman could achieve.

examples.japanese: 子どもならではの自由な発想に、大人たちは驚かされた。
examples.english: The adults were amazed by the free-spirited ideas that only a child could come up with.

meaning: in order to; with the aim of
structure: Verb-dict + べく (する → すべく)
usage: Formal written style; する usually becomes すべく. The main clause cannot be a request or command.

examples.japanese: 同社は海外市場に進出すべく、現地に新たな拠点を設けた。
examples.english: The company set up a new local base in order to expand into overseas markets.

examples.japanese: 彼は医師になるべく、働きながら夜間の予備校に通っている。
examples.english: In order to become a doctor, he attends an evening prep school while working.

examples.japanese: 被災地の復興を支援すべく、全国から多くのボランティアが集まった。
examples.english: Many volunteers gathered from all over the country to support the recovery of the disaster area.

meaning: if one were to (do), (something terrible would happen)
structure: Verb-volitional + ものなら
usage: Exaggerates the danger of an action. Not to be confused with 〜ものなら (N2), which takes the potential form for an unlikely wish: 行けるものなら行きたい.

examples.japanese: 父の前で母の料理に文句でも言おうものなら、大変なことになる。
examples.english: If I were to complain about Mom's cooking in front of Dad, there'd be hell to pay.

examples.japanese: この辺りは、少しでも雨が降ろうものなら、すぐに道路が冠水してしまう。
examples.english: Around here, if it rains even a little, the roads flood right away.

examples.japanese: 締め切りに一日でも遅れようものなら、二度と仕事をもらえなくなるだろう。
examples.english: If you were even one day late for the deadline, you'd never get work from them again.

pattern: 〜に至る / 〜に至って / 〜に至っては
meaning: reach; lead to; only when it came to; as for (the most extreme case)
structure: Noun / Verb-dict + に至る / Noun / Verb-dict + に至って / Noun + に至っては
usage: に至る: reach a (serious) point. に至って: only once things came to that. に至っては: introduces the most extreme example, usually negative. Related: 〜に至るまで 'down to, even'.

examples.japanese: 小さな行き違いが、ついには両社の提携解消にまで至った。
examples.english: A small misunderstanding eventually led all the way to the two companies dissolving their partnership.

examples.japanese: 死者が出るに至って、市はようやく危険な交差点の改良に乗り出した。
examples.english: Only after someone died did the city finally set about improving the dangerous intersection.

examples.japanese: 最近の若者は新聞を読まないと言われるが、弟に至ってはテレビのニュースさえ見ない。
examples.english: Young people today are said not to read newspapers, and as for my younger brother, he doesn't even watch the TV news.

meaning: cannot help feeling; cannot suppress (an emotion)
structure: Noun + を禁じ得ない
usage: Used with emotion nouns such as 怒り, 憤り, 同情, 驚き, 涙, 疑問. Formal; odd for trivial everyday feelings.

examples.japanese: 罪のない子どもたちが犠牲になったことに、深い憤りを禁じ得ない。
examples.english: I cannot help feeling deep outrage that innocent children have become victims.

examples.japanese: 長年の苦労の末に夢をかなえた彼の姿に、涙を禁じ得なかった。
examples.english: Seeing him realize his dream after years of hardship, I could not hold back my tears.

examples.japanese: 当局の対応の遅さには、疑問を禁じ得ない。
examples.english: I cannot help having doubts about how slowly the authorities responded.

meaning: be forced to; have no choice but to
structure: Noun + を余儀なくされる
usage: The noun is usually a suru-noun for an unwanted action (中止, 撤退, 変更, 入院). The active 〜を余儀なくさせる means 'force (someone) to'.

examples.japanese: 大型台風の接近により、多くの便が欠航を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: With a major typhoon approaching, many flights had to be canceled.

examples.japanese: 主力選手の相次ぐ負傷で、チームは戦術の大幅な変更を余儀なくされた。
examples.english: With key players injured one after another, the team was forced to change its tactics drastically.

examples.japanese: 住民たちは避難生活を余儀なくされ、今も仮設住宅で暮らしている。
examples.english: The residents were forced to evacuate and still live in temporary housing.

meaning: (only) possible because of; owe everything to
structure: Noun + あっての + Noun / Noun + あってのことだ
usage: AあってのB: B exists only thanks to A, so A is indispensable. Often expresses gratitude.

examples.japanese: お客様あっての商売ですから、どんな小さな声にも耳を傾けなければならない。
examples.english: Our business exists only because of our customers, so we must listen to even the smallest voice.

examples.japanese: 今日の私があるのも、支えてくれた家族あってのことだ。
examples.english: I owe who I am today to my family who supported me.

examples.japanese: 健康あっての人生だ。体を壊すまで働いてはいけない。
examples.english: Life is nothing without health. You mustn't work until you ruin your body.

meaning: depending on; regardless of
structure: Noun (+ の) + いかんで / Noun (+ の) + いかんによらず
usage: Very formal (いかん = 'how, what'). Variants: 〜いかんによって / いかんでは (depending on); 〜いかんにかかわらず / いかんを問わず (regardless of).

examples.japanese: 来季の契約は、今シーズンの成績いかんで決まる。
examples.english: Next season's contract will depend on this season's performance.

examples.japanese: 試験の結果いかんでは、留年もあり得る。
examples.english: Depending on the exam results, you might even have to repeat the year.

examples.japanese: 理由のいかんによらず、無断欠勤は認められない。
examples.english: Regardless of the reason, absence without notice will not be tolerated.

meaning: no matter (what, how); even if
structure: Verb-volitional + が / Verb-volitional + と / i-Adj stem + かろうが / na-Adj + だろうが / Noun + だろうが
usage: More emphatic than 〜ても; often with question words (何を, どこへ, いくら) or どんなに. The main clause shows the result is unaffected.

examples.japanese: 周りに何と言われようが、自分で決めた道を進むつもりだ。
examples.english: No matter what people around me say, I intend to follow the path I chose.

examples.japanese: どんなに忙しかろうと、彼は毎晩必ず子どもに絵本を読んでやる。
examples.english: No matter how busy he is, he never fails to read his child a picture book every night.

examples.japanese: 相手が上司だろうが、間違っていることははっきり指摘すべきだ。
examples.english: Even if it's your boss, you should clearly point out what's wrong.

pattern: 〜(よ)うが〜まいが / 〜(よ)うと〜まいと
meaning: whether or not; regardless of whether
structure: Verb-volitional + が + Verb-dict + まいが / Verb-volitional + と + Verb-dict + まいと
usage: The same verb is repeated. For ichidan verbs and する/来る, まい may attach to the nai-stem: 認めまい, しまい (or すまい), こまい.

examples.japanese: 君が賛成しようがしまいが、この計画はもう動き出している。
examples.english: Whether you agree or not, this plan is already in motion.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ろうと降るまいと、試合は予定どおり行われる。
examples.english: Rain or no rain, the match will be held as scheduled.

examples.japanese: 本人が認めようが認めまいが、証拠は明らかだ。
examples.english: Whether he admits it or not, the evidence is clear.

meaning: want to (do) but can't; even if one tries, one cannot
structure: Verb-volitional + にも + Verb-nai (potential of the same verb)
usage: Some outside circumstance blocks the intended action. The second verb is usually the negative potential of the same verb, or 〜ようがない.

examples.japanese: 財布を家に忘れてきたので、昼ご飯を買おうにも買えなかった。
examples.english: I'd left my wallet at home, so I couldn't buy lunch even though I wanted to.

examples.japanese: 大雪で電車が止まってしまい、帰ろうにも帰れない。
examples.english: The trains have stopped because of heavy snow, so I can't get home even if I want to.

examples.japanese: 当時の記録がすべて失われており、確かめようにも確かめようがない。
examples.english: All the records from that time have been lost, so there's no way to check even if we wanted to.

meaning: extremely; I feel so (emotion)
structure: i-Adj / na-Adj + な + かぎりだ
usage: Expresses the speaker's own strong feeling with emotion adjectives (うれしい, 寂しい, 心細い, うらやましい, 残念な). Not used for other people's feelings.

examples.japanese: 長年の夢だった自分の店をついに開くことができ、うれしいかぎりだ。
examples.english: I've finally opened my own shop, a long-held dream, and I couldn't be happier.

examples.japanese: 頼りにしていた先輩が来月で退職されるとは、心細いかぎりです。
examples.english: Hearing that the senior colleague I relied on is retiring next month leaves me feeling utterly lost.

examples.japanese: 若いのに三か国語を自在に操るなんて、うらやましいかぎりだ。
examples.english: So young and already fluent in three languages — I'm terribly envious.

meaning: while also; partly for the purpose of
structure: Noun + かたがた
usage: Formal; typically with お礼, ご挨拶, ご報告, お見舞い plus a verb of visiting (伺う, 訪ねる). Compare casual 〜がてら and 〜かたわら (parallel long-term activities).

examples.japanese: 先日のお礼かたがた、ご挨拶に伺いたいと存じます。
examples.english: I would like to call on you to pay my respects, and also to thank you for the other day.

examples.japanese: 退院のご報告かたがた、入院中のお見舞いのお礼を申し上げます。
examples.english: I'm writing to let you know I've left the hospital, and to thank you for visiting me there.

examples.japanese: 出張かたがた、久しぶりに恩師のお宅を訪ねた。
examples.english: While on a business trip, I also visited my former teacher's home for the first time in years.

meaning: just when one thought ...; contrary to expectation
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かと思いきや
usage: The outcome contradicts what was expected. Also 〜と思いきや. Found in lively writing and essays more than in speech.

examples.japanese: 今年の冬は暖かいかと思いきや、二月に入って記録的な大雪に見舞われた。
examples.english: We thought this winter would be mild, but then February brought record-breaking snow.

examples.japanese: 予約が取れないことで有名な店なので断られるかと思いきや、あっさり席が取れた。
examples.english: The restaurant is famous for being hard to book, so I expected to be turned down, but I got a table easily.

examples.japanese: 息子は宿題をしているのかと思いきや、机の下でゲームに夢中になっていた。
examples.english: I thought my son was doing his homework, but he was actually absorbed in a game under his desk.

meaning: have a (bad) tendency to
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai / Noun + の + きらいがある
usage: Always critical; common in commentary about people's habits or institutions. Compare conversational 〜がち and neutral 〜傾向がある.

examples.japanese: 彼は何事も自分一人で抱え込むきらいがある。
examples.english: He has a tendency to shoulder everything by himself.

examples.japanese: 最近の報道は、視聴者の不安をいたずらにあおるきらいがある。
examples.english: News coverage these days tends to stir up viewers' anxiety needlessly.

examples.japanese: この教授の論文は、結論を急ぎすぎるきらいがある。
examples.english: This professor's papers tend to rush to conclusions.

meaning: extremely; utterly
structure: na-Adj + 極まる / na-Adj + 極まりない
usage: Both mean the same; 極まりない is more common today. Mostly with negative na-adjectives (失礼, 危険, 不愉快, 退屈). 感極まる 'be overcome with emotion' is a set phrase.

examples.japanese: 公共の場で大声で電話をするなんて、迷惑極まりない。
examples.english: Talking loudly on the phone in a public place is extremely inconsiderate.

examples.japanese: 雨の夜に無灯火で自転車に乗るのは、危険極まりない行為だ。
examples.english: Riding a bicycle without a light on a rainy night is extremely dangerous.

examples.japanese: 被害者を嘲笑するような彼の発言は、不謹慎極まる。
examples.english: His remarks, which all but mocked the victims, were utterly inappropriate.

meaning: the height of; the utmost
structure: Noun + の極み
usage: Common with 光栄, 感激, 痛恨, ぜいたく, 疲労. Compare 〜の至り, which is limited to a few set phrases about the speaker's own feelings.

examples.japanese: 決勝戦であのような凡ミスをしたことは、まさに痛恨の極みだ。
examples.english: Making such a careless error in the final is the most bitter regret imaginable.

examples.japanese: 徹夜が三日続き、チームの全員が疲労の極みに達していた。
examples.english: After three all-nighters in a row, everyone on the team had reached the point of utter exhaustion.

examples.japanese: 一泊百万円のスイートとは、まさにぜいたくの極みだ。
examples.english: A suite costing a million yen a night is truly the height of luxury.

meaning: like; as; (after a person) the likes of
structure: Noun + の + ごとく / Verb-plain + (が) + ごとく / Noun + (の) + ごとき + Noun
usage: Literary equivalent of 〜ように / 〜ような. ごとき directly after a person shows contempt (お前ごとき) or, for oneself, humility (私ごとき).

examples.japanese: 彼女は何事もなかったかのごとく、静かに微笑んでいた。
examples.english: She was smiling quietly as if nothing had happened.

examples.japanese: 前述のごとく、本研究の対象は二十代の社会人に限定している。
examples.english: As stated above, this study is limited to working adults in their twenties.

examples.japanese: 私ごとき若輩者が、このような大役を務めてよいのでしょうか。
examples.english: Is it really all right for a novice like me to take on such an important role?

meaning: because; since (as an excuse or apology)
structure: Verb-plain / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + こととて
usage: Old-fashioned and formal, mainly in apologies or requests for understanding. Often with ぬ (知らぬこととて 'since I didn't know').

examples.japanese: 何分にも不慣れなこととて、至らぬ点があればご容赦ください。
examples.english: As I am still new to this, please forgive any shortcomings.

examples.japanese: 子どものしたこととて、今回ばかりは大目に見てやってください。
examples.english: It was a child who did it, so please overlook it just this once.

examples.japanese: 急なこととて、十分なおもてなしもできず失礼いたしました。
examples.english: It was all so sudden that I couldn't welcome you properly; please excuse me.

meaning: without (doing)
structure: Verb-dict + ことなしに
usage: Often followed by an impossibility ('without A, B cannot happen'). Close to 〜ことなく (N2), which simply means 'without doing'.

examples.japanese: 基礎を固めることなしに、応用力は身につかない。
examples.english: Without building a solid foundation, you will never develop the ability to apply what you know.

examples.japanese: 彼は誰にも相談することなしに、会社を辞めてしまった。
examples.english: He quit his job without consulting anyone.

examples.japanese: 痛みを伴うことなしに、この改革を成し遂げることはできない。
examples.english: This reform cannot be achieved without some pain.

meaning: end up (in a bad state); (things) have come to this
structure: Verb-dict + 始末だ / この + 始末だ
usage: A bad outcome after a series of events, told with exasperation. Often with とうとう, ついには, 挙げ句の果てに.

examples.japanese: 弟は遊んでばかりいて、とうとう単位が足りずに留年する始末だ。
examples.english: My brother did nothing but play, and he ended up having to repeat a year for lack of credits.

examples.japanese: 何度注意しても聞かず、ついには客の前で居眠りをする始末だった。
examples.english: He never listened to our warnings, and in the end he even dozed off in front of a client.

examples.japanese: あれだけ準備は万全だと言っていたのに、この始末だ。
examples.english: After all that talk about being fully prepared, look at this mess.

meaning: end up never doing; never got around to
structure: Verb-nai stem + ずじまい (する → せずじまい)
usage: Regret that an intended action never happened before the chance passed. Usually 〜ずじまいだった / 〜ずじまいになった.

examples.japanese: 旅行中は雨続きで、楽しみにしていた山には登らずじまいだった。
examples.english: It rained throughout the trip, so I never got to climb the mountain I'd been looking forward to.

examples.japanese: 忙しさに追われ、結局恩師にお礼を言わずじまいになってしまった。
examples.english: Swamped with work, I ended up never thanking my former teacher.

examples.japanese: 彼女の本当の気持ちは、とうとう聞けずじまいだった。
examples.english: In the end, I never got to hear how she really felt.

pattern: 〜ずにはおかない / 〜ないではおかない
meaning: will definitely (do); cannot fail to (cause a reaction)
structure: Verb-nai stem + ずにはおかない (する → せずにはおかない) / Verb-nai + ではおかない
usage: Two uses: firm resolve, or something that inevitably causes a feeling or reaction. Compare 〜ずにはいられない (N2), one's own irresistible urge.

examples.japanese: 彼女の力強い歌声は、聴く者の心を揺さぶらずにはおかない。
examples.english: Her powerful voice cannot fail to move the hearts of those who hear it.

examples.japanese: 今度という今度は、真相を突き止めずにはおかないぞ。
examples.english: This time I'm going to get to the bottom of it, no matter what.

examples.japanese: 政府の今回の決定は、国民の反発を招かずにはおかないだろう。
examples.english: The government's decision is bound to provoke a public backlash.

pattern: 〜ずにはすまない / 〜ないではすまない
meaning: must (do); won't get away without (doing)
structure: Verb-nai stem + ずにはすまない (する → せずにはすまない) / Verb-nai + ではすまない
usage: The obligation comes from social norms or the situation, not personal desire. 〜ずには済まされない is a stronger variant.

examples.japanese: 大切な花瓶を割ってしまったのだから、弁償せずにはすまないだろう。
examples.english: Since I broke that precious vase, I won't get away without paying for it.

examples.japanese: これほどの不祥事となれば、社長が責任を取らずにはすまない。
examples.english: With a scandal of this scale, the president will have to take responsibility.

examples.japanese: 取引先に迷惑をかけた以上、直接謝りに行かないではすまない。
examples.english: Since we caused our client trouble, we have to go and apologize in person.

meaning: as soon as (and again and again)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-ta + そばから
usage: A repeated pattern where the second action undoes the first, often with frustration. Unlike 〜や否や or 〜なり, it is not used for a single one-off event.

examples.japanese: 片付けるそばから、子どもたちがおもちゃを散らかしていく。
examples.english: As soon as I tidy up, the kids scatter their toys around again.

examples.japanese: 新しい単語は、覚えたそばから忘れてしまう。
examples.english: New words slip away as soon as I learn them.

examples.japanese: 母がクッキーを焼くそばから、弟がつまみ食いしてしまう。
examples.english: No sooner does my mother bake cookies than my little brother snacks on them.

meaning: not even (one); not a single
structure: Noun (一 + counter) + たりとも
usage: Attaches to 一 + counter (一円, 一日, 一人, 一瞬) and is followed by a negative or prohibition. Also 何人たりとも 'no one whatsoever'.

examples.japanese: 税金を一円たりとも無駄にしてはならない。
examples.english: Not a single yen of tax money must be wasted.

examples.japanese: 手術中は、一瞬たりとも気を抜くことができない。
examples.english: During an operation, you can't let your guard down for even an instant.

examples.japanese: 故郷で待つ家族のことを、一日たりとも忘れたことはない。
examples.english: I have never forgotten, even for a single day, the family waiting for me back home.

meaning: even (just); not even
structure: Verb-dict + だに / Noun + だに
usage: Archaic; survives mainly in set phrases: 想像するだに / 考えるだに ('just thinking about it'), 微動だにしない, 想像だにしない / 夢想だにしない ('never even imagine').

examples.japanese: あの事故の瞬間は、思い出すだに身震いがする。
examples.english: Just recalling the moment of that accident makes me shudder.

examples.japanese: 衛兵は一時間、微動だにせず立ち続けた。
examples.english: The guard stood for an hour without moving a muscle.

examples.japanese: 自分の書いた小説が映画化されるとは、想像だにしなかった。
examples.english: I never even imagined that a novel I wrote would be made into a film.

meaning: as (one in the position of); befitting
structure: Noun + たる + Noun / Noun + たるもの
usage: Stresses the duties or dignity expected of a role. 〜たる者 / 〜たるもの is followed by what such a person should (not) do.

examples.japanese: 教師たる者、生徒の前で模範を示さなければならない。
examples.english: Anyone who is a teacher must set an example in front of the students.

examples.japanese: 一国の首相たる人物が、このような軽率な発言をするとは嘆かわしい。
examples.english: It is deplorable that the prime minister of a nation would make such a careless remark.

examples.japanese: 王者たる風格が、彼の立ち姿から漂っていた。
examples.english: His very stance radiated the dignity of a true champion.

meaning: (doing) A and B alternately; back and forth
structure: Verb-stem + つ + Verb-stem + つ
usage: Only in set phrases with opposite verbs or active/passive pairs: 行きつ戻りつ, 持ちつ持たれつ, 抜きつ抜かれつ, 浮きつ沈みつ.

examples.japanese: 近所の人たちとは、持ちつ持たれつの関係でやってきた。
examples.english: My neighbors and I have always helped each other out.

examples.japanese: 彼は決心がつかず、店の前を行きつ戻りつしていた。
examples.english: Unable to make up his mind, he kept pacing back and forth in front of the shop.

examples.japanese: ゴール直前まで、二台の車は抜きつ抜かれつの接戦を繰り広げた。
examples.english: Right up to the finish, the two cars battled neck and neck, overtaking each other again and again.

meaning: whatever (it is); whoever; whether A or B
structure: Noun + であれ / Question word + であれ / Noun + であれ + Noun + であれ
usage: Written equivalent of 〜でも / 〜だろうと. 〜であろうと and 〜であろうが are close variants.

examples.japanese: 理由が何であれ、暴力は決して許されない。
examples.english: Whatever the reason, violence is never acceptable.

examples.japanese: 相手が誰であれ、礼儀をわきまえて接するべきだ。
examples.english: Whoever you're dealing with, you should treat them with proper courtesy.

examples.japanese: 正社員であれアルバイトであれ、安全研修は全員が受けなければならない。
examples.english: Whether full-time or part-time, everyone must take the safety training.

meaning: ought to; it would only be natural to
structure: Verb-te + しかるべきだ / i-Adj-ku + て + しかるべきだ / na-Adj + であって + しかるべきだ
usage: States what would be proper, often in the passive and often implying criticism that it hasn't happened. The adjective しかるべき also means 'appropriate'.

examples.japanese: これだけの損害を出したのだから、経営陣は責任を問われてしかるべきだ。
examples.english: Having caused this much damage, the management ought to be held accountable.

examples.japanese: 長年会社に貢献してきた彼女は、もっと評価されてしかるべきだ。
examples.english: Having contributed to the company for so many years, she deserves more recognition.

examples.japanese: 子どもの安全にかかわる問題なのだから、もっと早く対策が講じられてしかるべきだった。
examples.english: Since it concerns children's safety, measures should have been taken much sooner.

meaning: it's not as if (one were); since (one) is not
structure: Noun + ではあるまいし / Verb-dict + の + ではあるまいし
usage: Followed by a judgment, advice or command. Despite the formal まい, it's common in speech, especially as 〜じゃあるまいし.

examples.japanese: 子どもではあるまいし、自分のことくらい自分で決めなさい。
examples.english: You're not a child, so make your own decisions about yourself.

examples.japanese: 一生会えなくなるわけではあるまいし、そんなに泣かないで。
examples.english: It's not as if we'll never see each other again, so don't cry like that.

examples.japanese: 神様じゃあるまいし、未来のことなんか分かるわけがないよ。
examples.english: I'm not God, so there's no way I could know the future.

meaning: since (considering how it looks to others); out of consideration for
structure: Verb-plain / Noun + の + 手前
usage: Because of what one has said or one's position in front of others, one feels bound to act a certain way. Often followed by 〜わけにはいかない or 〜しかない.

examples.japanese: 部下の手前、上司の私が弱音を吐くことはできなかった。
examples.english: In front of my subordinates, I couldn't let myself complain as their boss.

examples.japanese: 必ず合格すると宣言した手前、今さら受験をやめるとは言えない。
examples.english: Having declared I would definitely pass, I can hardly say now that I'm giving up the exam.

examples.japanese: 子どもたちに約束を守れと言っている手前、親が約束を破るわけにはいかない。
examples.english: Since we tell our kids to keep their promises, we parents can't break ours.

meaning: it's all right to; there's no problem if
structure: Verb-te + もさしつかえない / i-Adj-ku + て + もさしつかえない / na-Adj + でもさしつかえない / Noun + でもさしつかえない
usage: A more formal 〜てもいい / 〜ても構わない, common in business, notices and official instructions. Often written 差し支えない.

examples.japanese: 書類は鉛筆で記入してもさしつかえありません。
examples.english: You may fill in the form in pencil.

examples.japanese: 急ぎの件でなければ、お返事は来週になってもさしつかえない。
examples.english: If it isn't urgent, it's fine if the reply comes next week.

examples.japanese: 応募資格は特にありませんので、未経験の方でもさしつかえありません。
examples.english: There are no particular requirements, so applicants with no experience are welcome.

meaning: because (of a special situation); as it is
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + とあって
usage: The cause is a special, noteworthy situation, and the main clause reports its natural, observed result. Common in news; not used for the speaker's own wishes or requests.

examples.japanese: 三連休の初日とあって、高速道路はどこも大渋滞だった。
examples.english: It being the first day of a three-day weekend, the expressways were jammed everywhere.

examples.japanese: 人気俳優が来店するとあって、店の前には早朝から長い行列ができた。
examples.english: With a popular actor coming to the store, a long line formed out front from early morning.

examples.japanese: 十年ぶりの再会とあって、二人は夜遅くまで語り合った。
examples.english: As it was their first reunion in ten years, the two talked late into the night.

meaning: if it's (for); if (such a special case) is so
structure: Verb-plain / Noun + とあれば
usage: A special condition under which one would make an exception or do something difficult. Frequently 〜のためとあれば.

examples.japanese: 子どもの命を救うためとあれば、どんな犠牲も惜しまない。
examples.english: If it's to save my child's life, I'll spare no sacrifice.

examples.japanese: 社長直々の頼みとあれば、断るわけにはいかない。
examples.english: If it's a request from the president himself, I can't refuse.

examples.japanese: 好きな作家のサイン会とあれば、多少遠くても行かずにはいられない。
examples.english: If it's a book signing by my favorite author, I can't not go, even if it's a bit far.

meaning: both A and B; in terms of A as well as B
structure: Noun + といい + Noun + といい
usage: Picks out two aspects as evidence for an overall evaluation, positive or negative. Unlike plain 〜も〜も, it carries the speaker's judgment.

examples.japanese: この旅館は、料理といい接客といい、申し分ない。
examples.english: This inn is flawless, both in its food and its service.

examples.japanese: 色といい形といい、この器は私の好みにぴったりだ。
examples.english: In color and shape alike, this bowl is exactly to my taste.

examples.japanese: 兄といい弟といい、あの家の息子たちはどうしてこうも時間にルーズなのだろう。
examples.english: The older brother and the younger one both — why are that family's sons so careless about time?

meaning: at most; about; more or less
structure: Noun / Verb-dict + といったところだ
usage: A rough, modest estimate: the amount or level isn't large. Often with せいぜい or まあ. Also 〜というところだ.

examples.japanese: 私の料理の腕前は、せいぜいカレーが作れるといったところだ。
examples.english: My cooking skills amount to making curry, at best.

examples.japanese: 通勤時間は、ドアからドアまで三十分といったところです。
examples.english: My commute is about thirty minutes door to door.

examples.japanese: 今年の売り上げは、ほぼ昨年並みといったところだ。
examples.english: This year's sales are more or less on par with last year's.

meaning: even though; even (someone like)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + といえども
usage: Formal version of 〜といっても / 〜であっても: even someone with that status is not exempt. Often with いかなる or たとえ.

examples.japanese: 子どもといえども、一人の人間として尊重されなければならない。
examples.english: Children too must be respected as individuals.

examples.japanese: いかなる権力者といえども、法の上に立つことは許されない。
examples.english: No one, however powerful, may stand above the law.

examples.japanese: 経験豊かなベテランといえども、この天候での登山は危険だ。
examples.english: Even for an experienced veteran, climbing in this weather is dangerous.

meaning: indescribably; extremely; beyond words
structure: i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + といったらない
usage: Works for both positive and negative feelings. Casual forms: 〜ったらない, and 〜といったらありゃしない (negative only).

examples.japanese: 決勝戦で一点差で負けたときの悔しさといったらなかった。
examples.english: The frustration of losing the final by a single point was beyond words.

examples.japanese: 新しい部屋から見る夜景の美しさといったらない。
examples.english: The night view from my new apartment is indescribably beautiful.

examples.japanese: あの人の話は同じことの繰り返しで、退屈といったらない。
examples.english: His talks just repeat the same thing over and over — they're unbelievably boring.

meaning: when it comes to; as for (complaint)
structure: Noun + ときたら
usage: Introduces a familiar person or thing the speaker is fed up with; what follows is a complaint. Conversational.

examples.japanese: うちの夫ときたら、休みの日は一日中ソファでごろごろしている。
examples.english: As for my husband, he lazes around on the sofa all day on his days off.

examples.japanese: 最近のテレビ番組ときたら、どの局も似たような内容ばかりだ。
examples.english: TV programs these days — every channel shows the same kind of thing.

examples.japanese: このパソコンときたら、肝心なときに限って固まってしまう。
examples.english: This computer always freezes right when I need it most.

pattern: 〜としたところで / 〜にしたところで
meaning: even if; even supposing; even for (someone)
structure: Verb-plain / Noun + としたところで / Noun + にしたところで
usage: Like 〜としても / 〜にしても, but stresses that the outcome won't change. Casual: 〜としたって / 〜にしたって.

examples.japanese: 今から急いだとしたところで、最終電車には間に合わないだろう。
examples.english: Even if we hurried now, we probably wouldn't make the last train.

examples.japanese: 部長にしたところで、この問題の解決策を持っているわけではない。
examples.english: Even the department manager doesn't have a solution to this problem.

examples.japanese: 仮に予算が倍になったとしたところで、人手が足りなければ計画は進まない。
examples.english: Even supposing the budget were doubled, the plan wouldn't move forward without enough staff.

meaning: (to think) that ...!; I'm surprised that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + とは
usage: Can end the sentence, leaving the reaction unsaid, or be followed by 思わなかった, 驚いた, etc. Different from definitional 〜とは ('X means ...').

examples.japanese: あの真面目な彼が、会社の金に手をつけていたとは。
examples.english: To think that someone as serious as him had been dipping into company money!

examples.japanese: 十年ぶりに訪れた故郷が、これほど様変わりしているとは思いもしなかった。
examples.english: I never imagined my hometown would have changed so much when I visited after ten years.

examples.japanese: 初めて出場した大会でいきなり優勝するとは、本人も驚いているに違いない。
examples.english: Winning the very first tournament she entered — she must be surprised herself.

meaning: as if to say
structure: Sentence + とばかりに
usage: Describes someone else's attitude or gesture that seems to say something without words; not used about oneself. Compare 〜んばかり (a nearly-reached extreme state).

examples.japanese: 店員は「早く帰れ」とばかりに、私たちのテーブルを片付け始めた。
examples.english: The waiter began clearing our table as if to say, 'Hurry up and leave.'

examples.japanese: 相手のミスを見て、彼はここぞとばかりに攻め込んだ。
examples.english: Seeing his opponent's mistake, he went on the attack as if to say, 'Now's my chance.'

examples.japanese: 息子は待ってましたとばかりに、誕生日プレゼントの包みを開けた。
examples.english: My son tore open his birthday present as if he'd been waiting for this very moment.

meaning: without meaning to; idly; (with question words) no particular
structure: Verb-dict + ともなく / Verb-dict + ともなしに / Question word + (particle) + ともなく
usage: The same verb is usually repeated (見るともなく見る). With question words: どこからともなく 'from nowhere in particular', 誰からともなく 'someone or other'.

examples.japanese: 電車の中で、隣の二人の会話を聞くともなく聞いていた。
examples.english: On the train, I was half-listening to the conversation of the two people next to me.

examples.japanese: 窓の外を見るともなしに眺めていると、雪がちらつき始めた。
examples.english: As I gazed idly out of the window, snow began to fall.

examples.japanese: どこからともなく、焼き魚のいい匂いが漂ってきた。
examples.english: From somewhere or other came the pleasant smell of grilled fish.

meaning: even if not (to that extent), at least
structure: Verb-nai + までも
usage: The first part names a high level not reached; the second a lower, acceptable level, often with せめて, 少なくとも or advice.

examples.japanese: 毎日とは言わないまでも、週に一度くらいは実家に電話しなさい。
examples.english: I won't say every day, but at least call home once a week.

examples.japanese: 優勝はできないまでも、せめて決勝までは勝ち進みたい。
examples.english: Even if we can't win the championship, I'd at least like to make it to the final.

examples.japanese: 完璧には理解できないまでも、大まかな流れはつかんでおくべきだ。
examples.english: Even if you can't understand it perfectly, you should at least grasp the general flow.

meaning: it's not impossible that; might (under some conditions)
structure: Verb-nai + ものでもない
usage: A roundabout, somewhat reluctant way to admit a possibility. Similar to 〜ないことはない (N3) but stiffer.

examples.japanese: 条件次第では、その仕事を引き受けないものでもない。
examples.english: Depending on the terms, I might be willing to take on the job.

examples.japanese: 今から全力で走れば、終電に間に合わないものでもない。
examples.english: If we run flat out now, it's not impossible we'll catch the last train.

examples.japanese: 彼の言い分も分からないものでもないが、やはり規則は規則だ。
examples.english: I can see his point to some extent, but rules are rules.

meaning: as (it was); while remaining; since (birth)
structure: Noun + ながらに / Noun + ながらの + Noun / Verb-stem + ながらに
usage: Limited to set expressions: 昔ながら, 涙ながら, 生まれながら, いつもながら, いながらにして ('without leaving one's place').

examples.japanese: この町には、昔ながらの手作りの和菓子屋が今も残っている。
examples.english: This town still has an old-fashioned shop that makes Japanese sweets by hand.

examples.japanese: 被害者の母親は、涙ながらに事件当日の様子を語った。
examples.english: The victim's mother tearfully described what happened on the day of the incident.

examples.japanese: 彼女は生まれながらに優れた音感を持っていた。
examples.english: She had an excellent ear for pitch from birth.

meaning: without (something essential), (cannot)
structure: Noun + なくして(は)
usage: Followed by a negative or impossibility; stresses that the noun is indispensable. More emphatic and literary than 〜なしに(は).

examples.japanese: 地域住民の理解なくして、この計画の成功はあり得ない。
examples.english: Without the understanding of local residents, this project cannot succeed.

examples.japanese: 失敗なくしては、本当の成長は得られない。
examples.english: Without failure, there can be no real growth.

examples.japanese: 多くの支援者の協力なくしては、この映画は完成しなかっただろう。
examples.english: Without the cooperation of many supporters, this film would never have been finished.

meaning: without
structure: Noun + なしに(は)
usage: なしに simply means 'without'; なしには is followed by a negative ('can't ... without'). Conversation often uses 〜なしで.

examples.japanese: 彼は何の連絡もなしに、三日間会社を休んだ。
examples.english: He stayed away from work for three days without any notice.

examples.japanese: 事前の許可なしには、この区域に立ち入ることはできません。
examples.english: You may not enter this area without prior permission.

examples.japanese: この話は、涙なしには聞けない。
examples.english: You can't listen to this story without shedding tears.

pattern: 〜ならいざしらず / 〜はいざしらず
meaning: it may be different for ..., but; I don't know about ..., but
structure: Noun + ならいざしらず / Noun + はいざしらず / Verb-plain + (の) + ならいざしらず
usage: The first case could be excused or is unknown; the actual case is judged more strictly. Close to 〜ならまだしも, but more literary.

examples.japanese: 子どもならいざしらず、大人がこんな簡単な漢字も読めないとは情けない。
examples.english: It would be one thing for a child, but it's shameful that an adult can't read such simple kanji.

examples.japanese: 昔はいざしらず、今の時代に手書きの履歴書にこだわる必要はないだろう。
examples.english: Things may have been different in the past, but nowadays there's no need to insist on handwritten résumés.

examples.japanese: 素人ならいざしらず、プロの料理人が塩と砂糖を間違えるなんて。
examples.english: Maybe for an amateur, but a professional chef mixing up salt and sugar?

meaning: if it were ..., it would be one thing (but)
structure: Noun + ならまだしも / Verb-plain + (の) + ならまだしも
usage: The first case is just about tolerable; the real situation is worse. More conversational than 〜ならいざしらず. Variant: 〜はまだしも.

examples.japanese: 一度ならまだしも、同じミスを三度も繰り返すのは問題だ。
examples.english: Once would be one thing, but repeating the same mistake three times is a problem.

examples.japanese: 遅刻するならまだしも、連絡もせずに休むのは社会人として失格だ。
examples.english: Being late is one thing, but skipping work without even calling is unacceptable for a working adult.

examples.japanese: 冗談で言うならまだしも、本気でそう思っているのなら問題だ。
examples.english: If you were joking, that'd be one thing, but if you really think that, it's a problem.

meaning: as soon as; the moment
structure: Verb-dict + なり
usage: Both actions are by the same (usually third-person) subject, and the second is often unexpected. Not for the speaker's own actions or future plans. Differs from 〜なり〜なり and 〜なりに.

examples.japanese: 娘は学校から帰ってくるなり、自分の部屋に閉じこもってしまった。
examples.english: The moment my daughter got home from school, she shut herself up in her room.

examples.japanese: 彼は受話器を取るなり、大声で怒鳴り始めた。
examples.english: As soon as he picked up the phone, he started shouting.

examples.japanese: 父は一口食べるなり、「懐かしい味だ」とつぶやいた。
examples.english: My father took one bite and immediately murmured, 'This tastes like the old days.'

meaning: either A or B; A or B or whatever
structure: Noun + なり + Noun + なり / Verb-dict + なり + Verb-dict + なり
usage: Gives sample options and is usually followed by a suggestion, request or command, not a past event. A single 〜なり can mean 'or something' (お茶なり).

examples.japanese: 分からないことがあれば、先生に聞くなり辞書で調べるなりしなさい。
examples.english: If there's something you don't understand, either ask your teacher or look it up in a dictionary.

examples.japanese: 週末は、映画なり買い物なり、好きなことをして過ごすといい。
examples.english: On the weekend, spend your time doing whatever you like — a movie, shopping, anything.

examples.japanese: 結果が出たら、電話なりメールなりで知らせてください。
examples.english: When the results come out, please let me know by phone, email or whatever.

meaning: in one's own way; as far as (one's limits) allow
structure: Noun + なりに / Noun + なりの + Noun / i-Adj + なりに / Verb-plain + なりに
usage: Accepts a limitation (age, ability, size) and says something is done or valued within it. Can sound condescending if used about a superior.

examples.japanese: 子どもは子どもなりに、親のことを心配しているものだ。
examples.english: Children, in their own way, worry about their parents.

examples.japanese: 自分なりに努力したつもりだが、結果は思わしくなかった。
examples.english: I thought I'd tried my best in my own way, but the results were disappointing.

examples.japanese: 狭い部屋には狭いなりの良さがある。
examples.english: A small room has its own merits precisely because it's small.

meaning: there's no need to; it's not worth (being surprised, etc.)
structure: Verb-dict + には当たらない / Noun + には当たらない
usage: Used with verbs of reaction: 驚く, 責める, 非難する, 心配する, 悲しむ, 賞賛する. The situation doesn't warrant that reaction.

examples.japanese: 彼の実力を考えれば、今回の優勝は驚くには当たらない。
examples.english: Considering his ability, his victory this time is nothing to be surprised about.

examples.japanese: 新人のうちは誰でも失敗するものだから、それほど責めるには当たらない。
examples.english: Everyone makes mistakes as a newcomer, so there's no need to blame him that much.

examples.japanese: 多少の遅れは想定内であり、心配するには当たらない。
examples.english: A slight delay was expected, so there's no cause for concern.

meaning: in (a situation or position); at (a time)
structure: Noun + にあって(は / も)
usage: A formal 〜で / 〜において that stresses being in a special situation. にあっても = 'even in'; にあっては = 'in (such a position)'.

examples.japanese: 物価が上がり続ける状況にあって、家計の見直しは避けられない。
examples.english: With prices continuing to rise, reviewing household finances is unavoidable.

examples.japanese: 彼女は逆境にあっても、決して笑顔を絶やさなかった。
examples.english: Even in adversity, she never stopped smiling.

examples.japanese: 責任ある立場にあっては、軽率な言動は慎むべきだ。
examples.english: When you're in a position of responsibility, you should refrain from careless words and actions.

meaning: it's not hard to (imagine, understand)
structure: Verb-dict + に難くない / Noun + に難くない
usage: Limited to a few words: 想像, 理解, 察する, 予想. Formal written style.

examples.japanese: 突然家族を失った遺族の悲しみは、想像に難くない。
examples.english: It is not hard to imagine the grief of those who suddenly lost their loved ones.

examples.japanese: 当時の彼がどれほど追い詰められていたかは、察するに難くない。
examples.english: It's easy to guess how cornered he must have felt at the time.

examples.japanese: この条件で工事を強行すれば、事故が起きることは予想に難くない。
examples.english: If construction is forced through under these conditions, it's easy to foresee an accident.

meaning: only (at/with); even for; being both A and B
structure: Noun + にして
usage: Main uses: a stage reached, often 〜にして初めて ('only at/with'); 'even for (someone exceptional)' (名人にしてなお解けない); and AにしてB 'both A and B'.

examples.japanese: 彼女は四十歳にして、初めて小説を書き上げた。
examples.english: She finished writing her first novel only at the age of forty.

examples.japanese: このような精密な作業は、熟練の職人にしてはじめて可能になる。
examples.english: Precision work like this is only possible in the hands of a seasoned craftsman.

examples.japanese: 彼は医師にして作家でもあり、多方面で活躍している。
examples.english: He is both a doctor and a writer, and is active in many fields.

meaning: in accordance with; based on (the facts, actual conditions)
structure: Noun + に即して / Noun + に即した + Noun
usage: Typical nouns: 事実, 実情, 現実, 実態, 状況. With laws or rules, 〜に則して or 〜に則って is used.

examples.japanese: 規則を機械的に当てはめるのではなく、実情に即して判断すべきだ。
examples.english: Rather than applying the rules mechanically, you should judge according to the actual circumstances.

examples.japanese: 本書は、実際の職場の場面に即した会話例を数多く取り上げている。
examples.english: This book features many sample conversations based on real workplace situations.

examples.japanese: 事実に即して報道することが、記者の最低限の責任である。
examples.english: Reporting in line with the facts is a journalist's most basic responsibility.

meaning: be worth (doing); unbearable to (see, hear); (feel) deeply
structure: Verb-dict + に堪える / Noun + に堪える / Verb-dict + に堪えない / Noun + に堪えない
usage: に堪える: 'worth (reading, seeing)'. Verb + に堪えない: 'too awful to (see, hear)'. Emotion noun + に堪えない (感謝, 遺憾): 'feel deeply', in formal speech.

examples.japanese: この作品は、大人の鑑賞にも十分堪える完成度の高いアニメだ。
examples.english: This is a polished anime that stands up well to viewing by adults too.

examples.japanese: 被災地の惨状は、見るに堪えないものだった。
examples.english: The devastation in the disaster zone was unbearable to look at.

examples.japanese: 皆様から温かいご支援をいただき、感謝に堪えません。
examples.english: I am deeply grateful for the warm support you have all given me.

meaning: worthy of; sufficient to
structure: Verb-dict + に足る + Noun / Noun + に足る + Noun
usage: Mostly before a noun (信頼に足る人物). The negative 取るに足らない ('trivial') is a common set phrase.

examples.japanese: 彼は、部下からも取引先からも信頼に足る人物だと評価されている。
examples.english: He is regarded by subordinates and clients alike as someone worthy of trust.

examples.japanese: 残念ながら、その主張を裏付けるに足る証拠は見つかっていない。
examples.english: Unfortunately, no evidence sufficient to support that claim has been found.

examples.japanese: 取るに足らないうわさなど、気にする必要はない。
examples.english: There's no need to worry about trivial rumors.

meaning: not limited to; not stopping at; going beyond
structure: Noun / Verb-plain + にとどまらず
usage: Stresses that something spreads beyond an expected scope or area. Close to 〜に限らず (N2) but with a stronger sense of expansion.

examples.japanese: 感染症の影響は一国にとどまらず、世界経済全体に及んだ。
examples.english: The impact of the epidemic was not confined to one country; it spread to the entire world economy.

examples.japanese: この運動は一時的なブームにとどまらず、社会の意識を大きく変えた。
examples.english: This movement was more than a passing fad; it greatly changed society's awareness.

examples.japanese: 彼の研究は、学問の世界にとどまらず、産業界からも注目を集めている。
examples.english: His research is drawing attention not only in academia but from industry as well.

meaning: in contrast to; unlike
structure: Noun + にひきかえ / Verb-plain + の + にひきかえ
usage: Contrasts two opposite things with the speaker's evaluation (one good, one bad). More subjective than 〜に対して.

examples.japanese: しっかり者の姉にひきかえ、妹はのんびり屋でいつも忘れ物ばかりしている。
examples.english: Unlike her dependable older sister, the younger one is easygoing and always forgetting things.

examples.japanese: 去年の猛暑にひきかえ、今年の夏はずいぶん過ごしやすい。
examples.english: In contrast to last year's scorching heat, this summer has been quite comfortable.

examples.japanese: 兄が勉強熱心なのにひきかえ、弟は漫画ばかり読んでいる。
examples.english: While the older brother is studious, the younger one does nothing but read manga.

meaning: even more than; above all
structure: Noun + にもまして / Question word + にもまして
usage: Often 以前にもまして, 例年にもまして. With a question word (何にもまして, 誰にもまして) it means 'more than anything / anyone'.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は、例年にもまして暑さが厳しい。
examples.english: The heat this summer is even more severe than usual.

examples.japanese: 合格の知らせは、何にもましてうれしかった。
examples.english: The news that I'd passed made me happier than anything.

examples.japanese: 前回にもまして、今回の選挙は投票率の低さが目立った。
examples.english: Even more than last time, this election stood out for its low turnout.

meaning: utmost; the height of (in set phrases)
structure: Noun + の至り
usage: Mostly in set phrases: 光栄の至り, 恐縮の至り, 感激の至り, and 若気の至り ('youthful folly'). Used in formal speeches and letters.

examples.japanese: このような席でご挨拶させていただけるとは、光栄の至りでございます。
examples.english: It is the greatest honor to be able to address you on such an occasion.

examples.japanese: 学生時代に派手な髪型をしていたのは、若気の至りだった。
examples.english: My flashy hairstyle in my student days was just youthful folly.

examples.japanese: 皆様にご迷惑をおかけし、誠に恐縮の至りです。
examples.english: I am truly sorry for having caused you all such trouble.

meaning: not only ... but also
structure: Noun / Verb-plain / i-Adj + のみならず / na-Adj + である + のみならず / Noun + である + のみならず
usage: Formal written equivalent of 〜だけでなく / 〜ばかりでなく. Can also open a sentence: のみならず、…

examples.japanese: この問題は日本のみならず、多くの先進国が抱える課題である。
examples.english: This issue is a challenge faced not only by Japan but by many developed countries.

examples.japanese: 彼女は優れた研究者であるのみならず、学生の指導にも熱心だ。
examples.english: She is not only an excellent researcher but also dedicated to mentoring students.

examples.japanese: 震災は建物を破壊したのみならず、住民の暮らしそのものを奪った。
examples.english: The earthquake not only destroyed buildings but took away the residents' very way of life.

meaning: let alone; not to mention
structure: Noun + はおろか
usage: AはおろかBも / さえ / まで: B is an even more basic case; usually about negative or surprising facts. Unlike 〜どころか, not used with commands or wishes.

examples.japanese: 足を骨折してしまい、走ることはおろか、歩くことさえままならない。
examples.english: I broke my leg, so I can barely even walk, let alone run.

examples.japanese: 祖父は海外はおろか、東京にも行ったことがない。
examples.english: My grandfather has never even been to Tokyo, let alone abroad.

examples.japanese: 給料日前で、外食はおろか、コンビニの弁当を買う余裕もない。
examples.english: It's right before payday, so I can't even afford a convenience-store bento, let alone eat out.

meaning: precisely because; only because
structure: Verb-ba + こそ / i-Adj stem + ければこそ / na-Adj + であればこそ / Noun + であればこそ
usage: Stresses a positive or well-meant reason, often to explain something that might be misunderstood. More literary than 〜からこそ.

examples.japanese: 君の将来を思えばこそ、厳しいことを言うのだ。
examples.english: It's precisely because I care about your future that I'm being so strict with you.

examples.japanese: 健康であればこそ、好きな仕事にも打ち込める。
examples.english: It's only because you are healthy that you can throw yourself into the work you love.

examples.japanese: 信頼していればこそ、この大役を彼女に任せたのです。
examples.english: It's precisely because I trust her that I entrusted her with this important role.

meaning: if ..., that's the end of it; it's all for nothing if
structure: Verb-ba + それまでだ
usage: Two uses: all effort is wasted if X happens; or 〜と言ってしまえばそれまでだ, 'saying X ends the discussion (but ...)'. Often with 〜てしまえば.

examples.japanese: どんなに高価な機械でも、壊れてしまえばそれまでだ。
examples.english: No matter how expensive a machine is, once it breaks, that's the end of it.

examples.japanese: いくら準備をしても、本番で緊張して何も言えなければそれまでだ。
examples.english: However much you prepare, if you freeze up and can't say anything on the day, it's all for nothing.

examples.japanese: 運が悪かったと言ってしまえばそれまでだが、防げた事故だったのではないか。
examples.english: You could just call it bad luck and leave it at that, but wasn't this an accident that could have been prevented?

meaning: must not; do not (on signs); (before a noun) must not be
structure: Verb-dict + べからず / Verb-dict + べからざる + Noun (する → すべからず)
usage: Archaic; mainly on signs, in rules and in set phrases. べからざる before a noun appears in 欠くべからざる ('indispensable') and 許すべからざる ('unforgivable').

examples.japanese: 境内の池のほとりには、「魚にえさを与えるべからず」と書かれた立て札がある。
examples.english: By the pond in the temple grounds stands a sign that reads, 'Do not feed the fish.'

examples.japanese: 彼の発言は、公職にある者として許すべからざるものだ。
examples.english: His remarks are unforgivable for someone holding public office.

examples.japanese: 水は人間の生活にとって欠くべからざるものである。
examples.english: Water is indispensable to human life.

meaning: cannot possibly; there's no way to
structure: Verb-dict + べくもない (する → すべくもない)
usage: Common with 望む, 知る, 比べる (also classical 比ぶべくもない). Literary; the impossibility comes from circumstances.

examples.japanese: プロの演奏と私の演奏とでは、比べるべくもない。
examples.english: There's no comparing a professional's performance with mine.

examples.japanese: 都心の一等地に家を買うなど、今の収入では望むべくもない。
examples.english: With my current income, buying a house in a prime central location is out of the question.

examples.japanese: 当事者が全員亡くなった今となっては、事故の真相は知るべくもない。
examples.english: Now that everyone involved has died, there is no way to know the truth about the accident.

meaning: unacceptable for (someone in that position); should not
structure: Noun + に + あるまじき + Noun / Verb-dict + まじき + Noun
usage: Mostly as 〜にあるまじき / 〜としてあるまじき + 行為, 発言, 態度: behavior unworthy of a role. Strongly critical and formal.

examples.japanese: 生徒に暴言を吐くなど、教育者にあるまじき行為だ。
examples.english: Verbally abusing students is conduct unbecoming of an educator.

examples.japanese: 賄賂を受け取るとは、政治家としてあるまじきことである。
examples.english: Accepting bribes is utterly unacceptable for a politician.

meaning: needless to; there's no need to (go as far as)
structure: Verb-dict + までもない
usage: The matter is too obvious or minor to need the action. 言うまでもなく ('needless to say') is a common set phrase.

examples.japanese: 言うまでもないが、試験中の私語は禁止だ。
examples.english: Needless to say, talking during the exam is prohibited.

examples.japanese: この程度の傷なら、わざわざ病院へ行くまでもない。
examples.english: A cut this minor isn't worth going all the way to the hospital for.

examples.japanese: 彼女の実力は、改めて説明するまでもないだろう。
examples.english: Her abilities hardly need explaining again.

meaning: (I'll) just (do); I merely (did)
structure: Verb-dict + までだ / Verb-ta + までだ / Verb-dict + までのことだ
usage: With Verb-dict: calm resolve to take the only remaining option. With Verb-ta: 'I only did X, nothing more', justifying one's action.

examples.japanese: 電車が動かないなら、歩いて帰るまでだ。
examples.english: If the trains aren't running, I'll just walk home.

examples.japanese: 今回だめでも、また来年挑戦するまでのことだ。
examples.english: Even if I fail this time, I'll simply try again next year.

examples.japanese: 別に怒っているわけではない。事実を言ったまでだ。
examples.english: I'm not angry. I was merely stating the facts.

meaning: covered in; smeared with
structure: Noun + まみれ
usage: Something (mud, blood, sweat, oil, dust, debt) sticks all over. Compare だらけ (lots of scattered things, even mistakes) and ずくめ (entirely, can be positive).

examples.japanese: 子どもたちは泥まみれになって、日が暮れるまで遊んでいた。
examples.english: The children played until sundown, getting covered in mud.

examples.japanese: 救助隊員は汗まみれになりながら、がれきの中を捜索し続けた。
examples.english: Drenched in sweat, the rescue workers kept searching through the rubble.

examples.japanese: 彼は事業に失敗して以来、借金まみれの生活を送っている。
examples.english: Ever since his business failed, he has been living a life buried in debt.

meaning: show signs of; become like; -ish
structure: Noun + めく / Noun + めいた + Noun
usage: Limited to certain nouns: 春めく, 秋めく, 謎めく, 皮肉めく, 冗談めく, 言い訳めく. More literary than 〜らしい / 〜っぽい.

examples.japanese: 三月に入り、日差しもだいぶ春めいてきた。
examples.english: Now that it's March, the sunlight has become quite spring-like.

examples.japanese: 彼女は謎めいた微笑みを浮かべて、何も答えなかった。
examples.english: She gave an enigmatic smile and said nothing.

examples.japanese: 先輩の皮肉めいた言い方が、どうも気になった。
examples.english: The slightly sarcastic way my senior colleague spoke kept bothering me.

meaning: not only ... but also (even more); ... aside
structure: Noun + もさることながら
usage: Acknowledges A, then stresses B as even more important or notable. Usually positive evaluations.

examples.japanese: この店は、料理の味もさることながら、器の美しさにも心を奪われる。
examples.english: At this restaurant, it's not just the flavor of the food — the beauty of the tableware captivates you too.

examples.japanese: 彼の成功は、才能もさることながら、人一倍の努力によるものだ。
examples.english: His success is due not only to talent but, even more, to his extraordinary effort.

examples.japanese: この本は内容もさることながら、装丁の美しさが話題を呼んだ。
examples.english: The book's content was good, but it was the beauty of its binding that got people talking.

meaning: if only (..., but); although (regret or reproach)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な + ものを
usage: Regret, dissatisfaction or reproach that things didn't go as they could have. Often with 〜ば / 〜たら; can end the sentence: 言ってくれればよかったものを.

examples.japanese: 一言相談してくれれば手伝ったものを、どうして一人で抱え込んだのか。
examples.english: If only you'd asked me, I would have helped — why did you keep it all to yourself?

examples.japanese: すぐに病院へ行けば軽く済んだものを、我慢したせいで入院する羽目になった。
examples.english: It would have been minor if he'd gone to the hospital right away, but because he put up with it, he ended up hospitalized.

examples.japanese: 黙っていればいいものを、彼は余計なことを言って話をこじらせた。
examples.english: He should have just kept quiet, but he said something unnecessary and complicated matters.

meaning: as soon as; the moment; no sooner ... than
structure: Verb-dict + や否や / Verb-dict + や
usage: The most written of the 'as soon as' group; past facts only, not intentions or commands. Also shortened to 〜や. Compare 〜なり (same subject) and 〜そばから (repeated).

examples.japanese: 首相が会見場に姿を現すや否や、一斉にカメラのフラッシュがたかれた。
examples.english: The moment the prime minister appeared in the press room, cameras flashed all at once.

examples.japanese: 新製品は発売されるや否や、たちまち品切れになった。
examples.english: No sooner had the new product gone on sale than it sold out.

examples.japanese: 終業のベルが鳴るや、生徒たちは教室を飛び出していった。
examples.english: As soon as the final bell rang, the students dashed out of the classroom.

meaning: because of; due to; therefore
structure: Noun + (の) + ゆえ(に) / Verb-plain + (が) + ゆえ(に) / i-Adj + (が) + ゆえ(に) / na-Adj + である + がゆえに
usage: Formal written 'because'; 〜がゆえに is emphatic and 〜ゆえの + Noun modifies a noun. At the start of a sentence, ゆえに means 'therefore' (logic, math).

examples.japanese: 若さゆえの無謀な挑戦だったが、今ではいい思い出だ。
examples.english: It was a reckless challenge born of youth, but now it's a fond memory.

examples.japanese: 彼は正直すぎるがゆえに、損をすることも多い。
examples.english: Because he is too honest, he often ends up losing out.

examples.japanese: 資源が乏しいがゆえに、この国は技術開発に力を注いできた。
examples.english: Precisely because it lacks resources, this country has poured its energy into technological development.

meaning: other than; apart from (no one / nothing else)
structure: Noun + をおいて(ほかに)〜ない
usage: Praises something as the only possible choice; followed by a negative (いない, ない). Unrelated to 置いて 'leave behind'.

examples.japanese: この難しい手術を任せられるのは、彼をおいてほかにいない。
examples.english: There's no one but him we can entrust with this difficult operation.

examples.japanese: 次の大会を開くなら、この町をおいてふさわしい場所はない。
examples.english: If we're holding the next tournament, there's no better place for it than this town.

examples.japanese: 今をおいて、改革を断行する機会はないだろう。
examples.english: If not now, there will be no other chance to push through reform.

meaning: starting with; beginning with (followed by a series)
structure: Noun + を皮切りに / Verb-plain + の + を皮切りに
usage: Marks the first of a series of similar events that expand or spread. Also 〜を皮切りとして.

examples.japanese: バンドは来月の東京公演を皮切りに、全国二十か所を回るツアーを行う。
examples.english: Starting with a concert in Tokyo next month, the band will tour twenty venues nationwide.

examples.japanese: 彼女の発言を皮切りに、会議ではさまざまな不満が噴き出した。
examples.english: Starting with her remarks, all sorts of complaints erupted at the meeting.

examples.japanese: この店は、駅前への出店を皮切りに、市内で次々と支店を増やしていった。
examples.english: Beginning with an outlet in front of the station, this shop opened one branch after another across the city.

meaning: taking the opportunity of; with (an event) as a turning point
structure: Noun + を機に / Verb-plain + の + を機に
usage: More formal than 〜をきっかけに (N2), usually for a significant turning point. Also 〜を機として.

examples.japanese: 還暦を機に、父は長年勤めた会社を退職した。
examples.english: On turning sixty, my father retired from the company he had worked at for decades.

examples.japanese: 子どもが生まれたのを機に、郊外の一戸建てに引っ越した。
examples.english: When our child was born, we took the opportunity to move to a house in the suburbs.

examples.japanese: 今回の事故を機に、社内の安全管理体制が全面的に見直された。
examples.english: Prompted by this accident, the company's safety management system was completely overhauled.

meaning: as of (and no longer); for the last time; at the top of (one's voice)
structure: Noun + を限りに
usage: Marks the last point before something ends (本日を限りに, 今回を限りに). 声を限りに 'as loud as one can' is a set phrase.

examples.japanese: 本日を限りに、当店は四十年の歴史に幕を下ろします。
examples.english: As of today, our shop closes its doors after forty years.

examples.japanese: 彼はこの試合を限りに、現役を引退すると発表した。
examples.english: He announced that this game would be his last before retiring.

examples.japanese: 遭難者は声を限りに助けを求めたが、誰にも届かなかった。
examples.english: The stranded climber cried out for help at the top of his voice, but no one heard him.

meaning: with; by means of; as of (a time)
structure: Noun + をもって
usage: Two uses: means (書面をもって, 実力をもって) and a formal end point (本日をもって). 〜をもちまして is common in announcements; 〜をもってすれば = 'with ..., (anything is possible)'.

examples.japanese: 以上をもちまして、本日の説明会を終了いたします。
examples.english: With that, we conclude today's information session.

examples.japanese: 選考の結果は、後日書面をもってお知らせいたします。
examples.english: The selection results will be sent to you in writing at a later date.

examples.japanese: 彼はその圧倒的な実力をもって、並み居る強豪を次々と打ち破った。
examples.english: With his overwhelming ability, he defeated one formidable rival after another.

meaning: in defiance of; undaunted by
structure: Noun + をものともせず(に)
usage: Admiring description of someone else overcoming a hardship; not used about oneself. Compare 〜をよそに (disregarding others' concern, often critical).

examples.japanese: 選手たちは激しい雨をものともせず、最後まで全力で戦い抜いた。
examples.english: Undaunted by the heavy rain, the players fought with all their might to the end.

examples.japanese: 彼女は周囲の反対をものともせず、単身で海外へ渡った。
examples.english: Undeterred by the objections of those around her, she went abroad alone.

examples.japanese: 救助隊は余震の危険をものともせずに、倒壊した建物に入っていった。
examples.english: Heedless of the danger of aftershocks, the rescue team went into the collapsed building.

meaning: ignoring; paying no heed to; oblivious to
structure: Noun + をよそに
usage: The noun is usually others' feelings or reactions (心配, 期待, 反対, 批判) that the subject disregards; often mildly critical.

examples.japanese: 親の心配をよそに、息子は連日夜遅くまで遊び歩いている。
examples.english: Heedless of his parents' worry, their son is out until late every night.

examples.japanese: 住民の反対をよそに、高層マンションの建設が始まった。
examples.english: Construction of the high-rise condominium began despite residents' opposition.

examples.japanese: 世間の騒ぎをよそに、当の本人はのんびりと釣りを楽しんでいた。
examples.english: Oblivious to all the public fuss, the man at the center of it was leisurely enjoying some fishing.

meaning: in order to; for the sake of (strong resolve)
structure: Verb-nai stem + んがため(に) (する → せんがため)
usage: Archaic and emphatic, expressing strong determination; not for trivial goals. 〜んがための + Noun modifies a noun.

examples.japanese: 彼は夢をかなえんがため、全財産をなげうって留学した。
examples.english: To realize his dream, he gave up everything he owned to study abroad.

examples.japanese: 勝たんがための卑劣な手段は、スポーツマンシップに反する。
examples.english: Resorting to underhanded tactics just to win goes against sportsmanship.

examples.japanese: 真実を明らかにせんがために、記者たちは危険を顧みず取材を続けた。
examples.english: To bring the truth to light, the reporters kept reporting regardless of the danger.

meaning: as if about to; almost (to the point of)
structure: Verb-nai stem + んばかり (する → せんばかり)
usage: A state so extreme something seems about to happen, though it doesn't. Forms: 〜んばかりに, 〜んばかりだ, 〜んばかりの + Noun. 言わんばかり overlaps with 〜とばかりに.

examples.japanese: 優勝が決まった瞬間、スタジアムは割れんばかりの拍手に包まれた。
examples.english: The moment the championship was decided, the stadium was filled with deafening applause.

examples.japanese: 彼女は今にも泣き出さんばかりの顔で、事情を説明した。
examples.english: Looking as though she might burst into tears at any moment, she explained what had happened.

examples.japanese: 課長は「君のせいだ」と言わんばかりに、私をにらみつけた。
examples.english: The section chief glared at me as if to say, 'This is your fault.'

meaning: now that; since (one must)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-ta + うえは
usage: Like 〜以上(は) and 〜からには (N2) but stiffer; the second half expresses resolve, obligation or advice. Also written 上は.

examples.japanese: 引き受けたうえは、最後まで責任を持ってやり遂げるつもりだ。
examples.english: Now that I've taken it on, I intend to see it through responsibly to the end.

examples.japanese: 契約を結んだうえは、条件は必ず守っていただきます。
examples.english: Now that the contract has been signed, we'll expect you to abide by its terms.

examples.japanese: こうなったうえは、正直にすべてを話すしかない。
examples.english: Now that it has come to this, there's nothing for it but to tell everything honestly.

meaning: only; just; nothing but
structure: ただ + Noun + のみ / ただ + Verb-dict + のみ
usage: Formal version of ただ〜だけ. Often ends a sentence as 〜のみだ ('all one can do is ...'). のみ alone also means 'only' in written style.

examples.japanese: 今はただ、手術の成功を祈るのみだ。
examples.english: All we can do now is pray that the operation succeeds.

examples.japanese: やるべきことはすべてやった。あとはただ結果を待つのみだ。
examples.english: I've done everything I should. All that's left is to wait for the results.

examples.japanese: この洞窟に入ることを許されたのは、ただ調査隊の隊員のみであった。
examples.english: Only members of the research team were allowed to enter this cave.

meaning: things like A and B (complaining list)
structure: Noun / Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + だの + ... + だの
usage: Lists examples with annoyance or disapproval, often followed by と(言う). Compare neutral 〜やら〜やら (N2) and 〜とか〜とか.

examples.japanese: 息子は、野菜は苦いだの肉は硬いだのと文句ばかり言って、なかなか食べない。
examples.english: My son keeps complaining that the vegetables are bitter, the meat is tough and so on, and hardly eats.

examples.japanese: 部屋の中は、古い雑誌だの壊れた家電だので足の踏み場もない。
examples.english: The room is so full of old magazines, broken appliances and whatnot that there's nowhere to step.

examples.japanese: 彼女は、疲れただの眠いだのと言って、なかなか宿題を始めない。
examples.english: Going on about being tired, being sleepy and so on, she just won't start her homework.

meaning: not hesitate to; openly (say, declare)
structure: Verb-te + はばからない
usage: With verbs of speaking (言う, 公言する, 断言する); often implies the boldness is excessive. Usually about a third person.

examples.japanese: 彼は自分こそが業界一の技術者だと公言してはばからない。
examples.english: He openly declares that he is the best engineer in the industry.

examples.japanese: その評論家は、現政権の政策を失敗だと断言してはばからない。
examples.english: That critic doesn't hesitate to call the current government's policies a failure.

examples.japanese: 監督は、このチームは必ず優勝すると言ってはばからなかった。
examples.english: The manager didn't hesitate to say that this team would definitely win the championship.

meaning: of all people; someone (of such standing) as
structure: Noun + ともあろう + Noun
usage: The noun is a respected role or institution; the sentence criticizes behavior unworthy of it. Usually 〜ともあろう者が / 人が.

examples.japanese: 警察官ともあろう者が、飲酒運転で捕まるとは。
examples.english: To think that a police officer, of all people, would be caught drunk driving!

examples.japanese: 一流ホテルともあろうものが、こんな初歩的なミスをするなんて信じられない。
examples.english: I can't believe a first-class hotel, of all places, would make such an elementary mistake.

examples.japanese: 大臣ともあろう人が、記者の質問から逃げるべきではない。
examples.english: Someone who is a government minister should not run away from reporters' questions.

meaning: using (something) as an excuse or pretext
structure: Noun + にかこつけて
usage: The stated reason is a pretext for what the person really wants to do. Close to 〜を口実に.

examples.japanese: 彼は出張にかこつけて、地方の温泉を巡っているらしい。
examples.english: Apparently he's been using business trips as an excuse to tour hot springs around the country.

examples.japanese: 体調不良にかこつけて、面倒な会議を欠席した。
examples.english: I used feeling unwell as an excuse to skip a tiresome meeting.

examples.japanese: 子どもの誕生日にかこつけて、自分が食べたかったケーキを買ってきた。
examples.english: Using my child's birthday as an excuse, I bought the cake I had wanted to eat myself.

meaning: if you ask (someone); in (someone's) opinion
structure: Noun + に言わせれば / Noun + に言わせると
usage: Introduces a personal, strongly held opinion that may differ from others'. Unlike neutral 〜によれば, it stresses the individual's view.

examples.japanese: 祖母に言わせれば、最近の若者は我慢が足りないそうだ。
examples.english: According to my grandmother, young people these days lack patience.

examples.japanese: 専門家に言わせれば、この程度の揺れで建物が倒れることはまずないという。
examples.english: If you ask the experts, a building is very unlikely to collapse from shaking of this level.

examples.japanese: 私に言わせれば、あの映画は評判ほど面白くない。
examples.english: If you ask me, that movie isn't as good as everyone says.

meaning: being too wrapped up in (to attend to other things)
structure: Noun + にかまけて
usage: The main clause names something neglected as a result; often self-critical or an excuse.

examples.japanese: 仕事にかまけて、家族と過ごす時間をおろそかにしてしまった。
examples.english: Wrapped up in work, I neglected the time I should have spent with my family.

examples.japanese: 新しいゲームにかまけて、試験勉強がまったく進んでいない。
examples.english: I've been so absorbed in a new game that I've made no progress studying for the exam.

examples.japanese: 育児にかまけて、自分の健康診断を何年も受けていなかった。
examples.english: Caught up in raising my kids, I hadn't had a health checkup for years.

meaning: despite (efforts); to no avail
structure: Verb-ta + かいもなく / Noun + の + かいもなく
usage: The effort did not pay off. The positive counterpart 〜かいがあって means 'the effort was worth it'. Also written 甲斐もなく.

examples.japanese: 家族の懸命な看病のかいもなく、祖父は静かに息を引き取った。
examples.english: Despite the family's devoted care, my grandfather passed away peacefully.

examples.japanese: 必死に練習したかいもなく、一回戦で敗退してしまった。
examples.english: For all our desperate practice, we were knocked out in the first round.

examples.japanese: 早起きして並んだかいもなく、目当ての限定品は目の前で売り切れた。
examples.english: Even though I got up early to line up, the limited item I wanted sold out right in front of me.

meaning: the most ... in; the best in
structure: Noun + きっての + Noun
usage: The noun is a group or place (社内, 町内, 学校, 業界, 国内). Used for praise, usually of a person or an establishment.

examples.japanese: 彼女は社内きっての切れ者として知られている。
examples.english: She is known as the sharpest mind in the company.

examples.japanese: この旅館は、温泉街きっての老舗だ。
examples.english: This inn is the most venerable establishment in the hot spring town.

examples.japanese: 学年きっての秀才と言われた兄も、社会に出てからは苦労している。
examples.english: My brother, once called the brightest student in his year, has struggled since starting work.

meaning: even without; without having to
structure: Verb-nai stem + ずとも (する → せずとも)
usage: Literary version of 〜なくても. 〜ずともよい means 'need not'.

examples.japanese: わざわざ言わずとも、彼なら状況を察してくれるだろう。
examples.english: Even without my spelling it out, he'll probably grasp the situation.

examples.japanese: これくらいの距離なら、車を使わずとも歩いて行ける。
examples.english: At this distance, you can walk there without taking the car.

examples.japanese: 急がずとも、会議にはまだ十分間に合いますよ。
examples.english: Even if we don't hurry, we'll still be in plenty of time for the meeting.

meaning: although; even though; that said
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + とはいえ
usage: Admits a fact, then says the expected result doesn't fully follow. Can open a sentence ('that said'). More formal than 〜といっても.

examples.japanese: 春とはいえ、朝晩はまだ冷え込む。
examples.english: Although it's spring, mornings and evenings are still cold.

examples.japanese: 締め切りまで一か月あるとはいえ、そろそろ準備を始めたほうがいい。
examples.english: Even though there's a month until the deadline, you'd better start preparing soon.

examples.japanese: 景気は回復傾向にある。とはいえ、中小企業の経営は依然として厳しい。
examples.english: The economy is on a recovery trend. That said, small and medium-sized businesses are still struggling.

meaning: as was bound to happen; inevitably
structure: Verb-dict + べくして + Verb-ta (same verb)
usage: The same verb is repeated (起こるべくして起こる); the outcome was the natural consequence of the circumstances.

examples.japanese: 安全点検を怠っていたのだから、あの事故は起こるべくして起こったと言える。
examples.english: Since safety inspections had been neglected, you could say that accident was bound to happen.

examples.japanese: 誰よりも練習を重ねてきた彼女は、勝つべくして勝ったのだ。
examples.english: Having practiced harder than anyone, she won, just as she was bound to.

examples.japanese: もともと無理のある計画だったので、失敗すべくして失敗した。
examples.english: It was an unrealistic plan from the start, so it failed as it was bound to.

meaning: smack of; seem like (in a bad way); -ish
structure: Noun + じみる / Noun + じみた + Noun
usage: Negative nuance: 子どもじみた, 年寄りじみた, 説教じみた, 芝居じみた. Compare neutral 〜めく and casual 〜っぽい. With 汗 or 油 it means 'stained with'.

examples.japanese: いい大人が、そんな子どもじみた言い訳をするものではない。
examples.english: A grown adult shouldn't make such childish excuses.

examples.japanese: 彼の話はどこか説教じみていて、素直に聞く気になれない。
examples.english: The way he talks is somehow preachy, so I can't bring myself to listen with an open mind.

examples.japanese: 彼はまだ二十代なのに、年寄りじみたことばかり言う。
examples.english: He's still in his twenties, yet he talks like an old man.

meaning: including all; the whole (group) together
structure: Noun + ぐるみ
usage: Works with a limited set of nouns: 家族, 町, 地域, 会社, 組織, 身ぐるみ. 会社ぐるみ / 組織ぐるみ often describe organized wrongdoing.

examples.japanese: 隣の家とは、家族ぐるみで付き合っている。
examples.english: Our whole family is close with the family next door.

examples.japanese: この地域では、町ぐるみで子どもたちの登下校を見守っている。
examples.english: In this area, the whole town watches over the children on their way to and from school.

examples.japanese: 調査の結果、会社ぐるみの不正であったことが明らかになった。
examples.english: The investigation revealed that the fraud involved the entire company.

meaning: there's a limit to; too ... (beyond what's acceptable)
structure: Noun / na-Adj / i-Adj / Verb-dict + にもほどがある
usage: Strong criticism or indignation that something has gone too far. Conversational and emotional.

examples.japanese: 約束の時間に二時間も遅れてくるなんて、非常識にもほどがある。
examples.english: Showing up two hours late for an appointment — there's a limit to how inconsiderate you can be.

examples.japanese: 初対面の人に年収を聞くなんて、失礼にもほどがある。
examples.english: Asking someone's income the first time you meet them is beyond rude.

examples.japanese: 冗談にもほどがある。そんな話、誰が信じるものか。
examples.english: That's taking a joke too far. Who would ever believe a story like that?

meaning: taking (unfair) advantage of; using (a situation) as license to
structure: Noun + をいいことに / Verb-plain + の + をいいことに
usage: Critical: someone exploits a situation to do something improper. For a neutral 'taking the opportunity', use 〜を機に or 〜をきっかけに.

examples.japanese: 親が留守なのをいいことに、息子は友達を呼んで夜通し騒いでいた。
examples.english: Taking advantage of his parents being away, the son invited friends over and partied all night.

examples.japanese: 上司が何も言わないのをいいことに、彼は毎日のように遅刻してくる。
examples.english: Taking advantage of the fact that his boss never says anything, he comes in late almost every day.

examples.japanese: 高齢者の知識不足をいいことに、業者は高額な契約を結ばせていた。
examples.english: Exploiting elderly people's lack of knowledge, the dealer had been getting them to sign expensive contracts.

meaning: in accordance with (rules, law, tradition)
structure: Noun + に則って / Noun + に則った + Noun
usage: The noun is a norm or model: 法律, 規則, 伝統, しきたり, 手順. Compare 〜に即して, used with facts and actual conditions.

examples.japanese: 大会は、国際ルールに則って公正に運営される。
examples.english: The tournament will be run fairly in accordance with international rules.

examples.japanese: 二人の結婚式は、古くからのしきたりに則って神社で執り行われた。
examples.english: Their wedding was held at a shrine according to long-standing custom.

examples.japanese: 本件については、社内規定に則った処分が下される予定だ。
examples.english: In this matter, disciplinary action in line with company regulations is expected.

meaning: whether A or B; A or B alike (fixed pairs)
structure: i-Adj stem + かれ + i-Adj stem + かれ
usage: A classical adjective form surviving only in fixed opposite pairs: 遅かれ早かれ, 多かれ少なかれ, 良かれあしかれ. Not productive.

examples.japanese: 遅かれ早かれ、この秘密はみんなに知られることになるだろう。
examples.english: Sooner or later, everyone will probably find out this secret.

examples.japanese: 多かれ少なかれ、誰にでも人に言えない悩みはあるものだ。
examples.english: Everyone has worries they can't share with others, to a greater or lesser degree.

examples.japanese: 良かれあしかれ、あの人の一言が会社の方向を決めてきた。
examples.english: For better or worse, a single word from that man has set the company's course.

meaning: extremely; nothing could be more
structure: i-Adj + ことこの上ない / na-Adj + な + ことこの上ない
usage: A stiff, written way to say 'extremely'. Also この上ない + Noun (この上ない喜び 'the greatest joy'). Close to 〜極まりない.

examples.japanese: 深夜の山道を一人で運転するのは、心細いことこの上ない。
examples.english: Driving alone on a mountain road late at night is as unnerving as it gets.

examples.japanese: 彼の説明は回りくどく、分かりにくいことこの上ない。
examples.english: His explanation is roundabout and extremely hard to follow.

examples.japanese: 会議中に何度も携帯電話が鳴り、迷惑なことこの上なかった。
examples.english: A cell phone kept ringing during the meeting, which was extremely annoying.

meaning: it seems (judging from evidence); apparently
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + とみえる / Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + とみえて
usage: An inference from what one observes; with 〜とみえて the observed evidence follows. More literary than 〜らしい / 〜ようだ. Also written と見える.

examples.japanese: 息子はよほど疲れていたとみえて、夕食も食べずに眠ってしまった。
examples.english: My son must have been really tired — he fell asleep without even eating dinner.

examples.japanese: 隣の家は留守とみえて、何度チャイムを鳴らしても返事がない。
examples.english: The neighbors seem to be out; nobody answers no matter how many times I ring the bell.

examples.japanese: 彼はこの結果にかなり満足しているとみえる。
examples.english: He seems to be quite satisfied with this result.

meaning: based on; taking into account; in light of
structure: Noun + を踏まえて / Noun + を踏まえた + Noun
usage: Common in business and official writing. Unlike 〜に基づいて (N2), which follows a basis closely, it means building on or reflecting something.

examples.japanese: アンケートの結果を踏まえて、来年度のサービス内容を見直すことにした。
examples.english: Based on the survey results, we decided to review next year's service offerings.

examples.japanese: 過去の失敗を踏まえたうえで、新たな計画を立てるべきだ。
examples.english: We should draw up a new plan that takes our past failures into account.

examples.japanese: 委員会は現地調査の結果を踏まえ、報告書をまとめた。
examples.english: The committee compiled its report in light of the findings of its on-site investigation.

meaning: it's not impossible that; there's a chance that
structure: Verb-nai + とも限らない
usage: Warns of a small but real possibility, usually undesirable, and is often followed by a precaution. Different from 〜とは限らない ('not necessarily').

examples.japanese: 途中で渋滞に巻き込まれないとも限らないから、早めに出発しよう。
examples.english: We might get stuck in traffic on the way, so let's leave early.

examples.japanese: 誰が聞いていないとも限らないので、ここで仕事の話はやめておこう。
examples.english: You never know who might be listening, so let's not talk about work here.

examples.japanese: 大きな地震がいつ起きないとも限らない。日頃から備えておくことが大切だ。
examples.english: A major earthquake could strike at any time, so it's important to be prepared every day.
